articles.title: How to test whether a QR destination works without a session
articles.excerpt: A QR code can decode correctly and still send a new visitor to a login page. Test the destination independently of the device that created the code. Open the exact URL encoded in the QR code in a fres…
articles.body: A QR code can decode correctly and still send a new visitor to a login page. Test the destination independently of the device that created the code. Open the exact URL encoded in the QR code in a fresh browser profile or a private window. Follow any redirects and check the final hostname and page. If the visible result depends on JavaScript, load the page in a browser and check the actual content. An HTTP 200 is useful evidence, but a sign-in page can also return 200. For a repeatable command-line check, use curl -sS -L -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code} %{url_effective}\n' ' https://example.com/menu '. Replace the sample address with your URL. This tells you the status and effective URL after HTTP redirects. It does not establish that a browser visitor can see the intended content.

articles.title: AI Makes Migrations Faster. It Doesn't Make Them Easy.
articles.excerpt: By Penko Vasilev, Principal Databricks Architect at Cosmos Thrace. Reviewed by Ivan Angelinin, Technical Director. “AI changes how fast we write the code. It doesn't change what makes a migration succ…
articles.body: By Penko Vasilev, Principal Databricks Architect at Cosmos Thrace. Reviewed by Ivan Angelinin, Technical Director. “AI changes how fast we write the code. It doesn't change what makes a migration succeed or fail.” TL;DR AI changes how fast we write the code. It doesn't change what makes a migration succeed or fail. First decide whether it is a lift and shift or a lift and modernize. “We rewrote it with AI in six weeks” usually describes a lift and shift. What slows migrations down is business meaning, not technology. AI can tell you what the code does, not why. Write the mapping before the code. Business owners can sign off on a mapping. They can't sign off on 40,000 lines of generated code. Validate automatically: row counts, totals and record-by-record differences.

articles.body: Small ICMP pings succeed, an SSH login prompt appears, and then the session freezes the moment a directory listing or TLS certificate crosses the tunnel. When control traffic works and larger payloads hang, encapsulation overhead has usually pushed packets past the path MTU while Path MTU Discovery (PMTUD) is blocked. Every tunnel wraps the original packet in extra headers. On a 1,500-byte Ethernet link, those outer headers eat directly into what the inner packet can carry. Subtracting WireGuard overhead byte by byte Take a standard WireGuard tunnel running over IPv4 on a 1,500-byte underlay.

articles.title: How I Built a Pre-Merge SSR SEO Audit Gate for Next.js 16 Content Pages
articles.excerpt: When you ship programmatic or template-driven content pages in Next.js, next build and ESLint will happily pass while your pages quietly fail in Google Search Console as "Crawled - currently not index…
articles.body: When you ship programmatic or template-driven content pages in Next.js, next build and ESLint will happily pass while your pages quietly fail in Google Search Console as "Crawled - currently not indexed." I ran into this firsthand while building and scaling structured reference pages for Tarot Fortune Cards on Next.js 16 (App Router) + React 19 + next-intl . The UI looked great in Chrome, Lighthouse was green, and every route compiled cleanly—yet inspecting the raw HTML that crawlers actually receive exposed four subtle bugs that were silently hurting indexation. Instead of doing manual spot-checks after deployment, I turned those failure modes into an automated two-stage pre-merge SEO gate (static repo check + live Vercel preview SSR HTML check).

articles.body: Sports in space have a long and proud tradition, whether it's Alan Shepard playing golf on the moon or the crew of the ISS hosting their own version of the Summer Olympics . articles.title: On this day in space! Nov. 23, 2015: Blue Origin sticks 1st-ever rocket landing from space with its suborbital New Shepard rocket
articles.excerpt: On Nov. 23, 2015, a Blue Origin rocket made a historic landing after launching into suborbital space. Here's why it mattered.
articles.body: On Nov. 23, 2015, a Blue Origin rocket made a historic landing. Before this time, all rockets were single-use only — even SpaceX's rockets. Blue Origin changed the concept forever. After launching the New Shepard capsule safely into space, the rocket started heading back to Earth. It flew towards a landing pad, reignited its engine to slow down and touched down softly on the ground . This was the first successful vertical landing from space in history. The Blue Origin milestone meant that rockets could be reused for multiple missions, which saves money and reduces waste. (Image credit: Blue Origin) Why it mattered Today, SpaceX may be the most well-known for landing its Falcon 9 rocket boosters from orbit.

articles.title: Weird 'potato chips' and 'ghostly rocks' on Mars spotted by NASA rovers Curiosity and Perseverance
articles.excerpt: These strange geological features may offer clues to the Red Planet's watery past.
articles.body: NASA's Curiosity and Perseverance rovers have spotted a bizarre assortment of Martian oddities, from potato chip-like rocks and ghostly white formations to mysterious patterns etched into the Red Planet's surface. While their appearances may be unusual, these formations offer scientists something far more valuable than a collection of curious snapshots: clues to the geological processes that shaped Mars over billions of years. In particular, the rocks and mineral deposits could help researchers piece together the planet's watery past and identify environments that may once have been capable of supporting microbial life.

articles.title: 'Avengers: Doomsday' gets final trailer, explaining why Steve Rogers is back and showing an epic battle with the X-Men
articles.excerpt: Marvel Studios’ first Avengers film since 2019 is less than a month away, and it might be the big-screen team-up event we thought impossible only ten years ago.
articles.body: The final trailer for Avengers: Doomsday just landed, and it finally puts the spotlight on our boy Steve Rogers. Avengers: Doomsday has been promising the scale and excitement the MCU has often been lacking since the Infinity Saga. Previous trailers played it safe, mostly setting up the conflict and introducing Victor Von Doom. Now it’s time for one last explosive look at the film before it tries to conquer cinemas next month. Disney and Marvel Studios have just released a "final trailer" that puts the focus back on Steve Rogers — no longer Captain America but still ready to use Mjolnir — and Thor as the veterans leading the New Avengers, former colleagues, the Fantastic Four, and even Fox's X-Men (after some first-encounter fights, of course) against Doom and his followers.
